title: The most feared song in jazz, explained
speaker: Vox
zh: 【Vox】解釋說，爵士樂中最令人恐懼的歌曲（精選雙語跟讀教材）

cues.text: This is John Coltrane’s Giant Steps. It’s considered one of the most important
cues.en: This is John Coltrane’s Giant Steps. It’s considered one of the most important
cues.zh: 這是約翰‧柯特蘭的《巨型階梯》。它被認為是最重要的之一

cues.text: jazz albums of all time, it cemented John Coltrane as a legend among
cues.en: jazz albums of all time, it cemented John Coltrane as a legend among
cues.zh: 有史以來的爵士樂專輯，它鞏固了約翰·科爾特蘭 (John Coltrane) 的傳奇地位

cues.text: jazz saxophonists and composers, and it’s home to one of the most one of the most revered and feared compositions in jazz history.
cues.en: jazz saxophonists and composers, and it’s home to one of the most one of the most revered and feared compositions in jazz history.
cues.zh: 它是爵士樂歷史上最受尊敬和最令人畏懼的作品之一的故鄉。

cues.text: The reason why the album's title track is so iconic can be heard in its first few seconds.
cues.en: The reason why the album's title track is so iconic can be heard in its first few seconds.
cues.zh: 專輯的主打歌如此具有標誌性的原因可以在最初的幾秒鐘內聽出來。

cues.text: Coltrane wrote these unique chord changes for Giant Steps, and later went on to use
cues.en: Coltrane wrote these unique chord changes for Giant Steps, and later went on to use
cues.zh: Coltrane 為 Giant Steps 創作了這些獨特的和絃變化，後來繼續使用

cues.text: them over traditional jazz standards.
cues.en: them over traditional jazz standards.
cues.zh: 他們超越了傳統的爵士樂標準。

cues.text: These chords came to be known as the Coltrane Changes -- and improvising over them is considered a rite
cues.en: These chords came to be known as the Coltrane Changes -- and improvising over them is considered a rite
cues.zh: 這些和絃後來被稱為 Coltrane Changes——即興演奏它們被認為是一種儀式

cues.text: of passage for jazz musicians.
cues.en: of passage for jazz musicians.
cues.zh: 爵士音樂家的段落。

cues.text: But, if you don’t understand a lick of music theory like me, it’s really hard to see
cues.en: But, if you don’t understand a lick of music theory like me, it’s really hard to see
cues.zh: 但是，如果你跟我一樣不懂一點樂理的話，真的很難看出來

cues.text: how this is so legendary.
cues.en: how this is so legendary.
cues.zh: 這怎麼這麼傳奇。

cues.text: Lucky for me, I know two people that can explain why…
cues.en: Lucky for me, I know two people that can explain why…
cues.zh: 對我來說幸運的是，我認識兩個人可以解釋為什麼...

cues.text: Braxton Cook Braxton: Okay you caught me off guard there!
cues.en: Braxton Cook Braxton: Okay you caught me off guard there!
cues.zh: 布拉克斯頓庫克布拉克斯頓：好吧，你讓我措手不及！

cues.text: And Adam Neely Adam: Should I get into the, like, technical jargony stuff?
cues.en: And Adam Neely Adam: Should I get into the, like, technical jargony stuff?
cues.zh: Adam Neely Adam：我應該瞭解技術術語之類的東西嗎？

cues.text: Let’s cut to the logo first.
cues.en: Let’s cut to the logo first.
cues.zh: 讓我們先切入徽標。

cues.text: So there’s a moment in the Giant Steps recording that really illustrates just how demanding
cues.en: So there’s a moment in the Giant Steps recording that really illustrates just how demanding
cues.zh: 因此，《Giant Steps》錄音中的一個時刻真正說明瞭要求有多高

cues.text: this song is.
cues.en: this song is.
cues.zh: 這首歌是。

cues.text: It happens when Tommy Flanagan, the pianist on the record, starts his solo.
cues.en: It happens when Tommy Flanagan, the pianist on the record, starts his solo.
cues.zh: 當唱片中的鋼琴家湯米·弗拉納根開始獨奏時，就會發生這種情況。

cues.text: Braxton: The story goes that John Coltrane brought in the music, he shows up ready to
cues.en: Braxton: The story goes that John Coltrane brought in the music, he shows up ready to
cues.zh: 布拉克斯頓：據說約翰·科爾特蘭帶來了音樂，他現身準備好

cues.text: go and then calls he this really fast tempo.
cues.en: go and then calls he this really fast tempo.
cues.zh: 去然後說他節奏真快。

cues.text: Adam: If you hear on the recording, Tommy Flanagan just cannot handle
cues.en: Adam: If you hear on the recording, Tommy Flanagan just cannot handle
cues.zh: 亞當：如果你在錄音中聽到，湯米·弗拉納根就是無法應對

cues.text: the chord progressions as they're going by. His improvisation is very halted.
cues.en: the chord progressions as they're going by. His improvisation is very halted.
cues.zh: 和絃進行時的情況。他的即興創作非常停滯。

cues.text: Braxton: And Tommy Flannagan's just holding on for dear life.
cues.en: Braxton: And Tommy Flannagan's just holding on for dear life.
cues.zh: 布拉克斯頓：湯米·弗蘭納根（Tommy Flannagan）只是為了寶貴的生命而堅持下去。

cues.text: It really becomes apparent how much he struggled, when you hear Coltrane take off at lightning
cues.en: It really becomes apparent how much he struggled, when you hear Coltrane take off at lightning
cues.zh: 當你聽到 Coltrane 閃電般起飛時，你可以明顯看出他是多麼掙扎

cues.text: speed the second Flanagan stops.
cues.en: speed the second Flanagan stops.
cues.zh: 第二個弗拉納根停止時的速度。

cues.text: Braxton: And then it goes down as like one of the most legendary recordings of all time. That’s messed up. I’d want another shot. I’d be like bro, don’t put that recording out.
cues.en: Braxton: And then it goes down as like one of the most legendary recordings of all time. That’s messed up. I’d want another shot. I’d be like bro, don’t put that recording out.
cues.zh: 布拉克斯頓：然後它就成為有史以來最具傳奇色彩的唱片之一。那真是一團糟。我還想再拍一次。我會像兄弟一樣，不要把錄音拿出來。

cues.text: To understand why this was so difficult for even a highly trained pianist, we need to know
cues.en: To understand why this was so difficult for even a highly trained pianist, we need to know
cues.zh: 要理解為什麼即使對於訓練有素的鋼琴家來說這也是如此困難，我們需要知道

cues.text: three basic concepts and it all starts with this: the circle of fifths - it’s kind of like
cues.en: three basic concepts and it all starts with this: the circle of fifths - it’s kind of like
cues.zh: 三個基本概念，這一切都始於：五度圈 - 有點像

cues.text: a color wheel for music.
cues.en: a color wheel for music.
cues.zh: 音樂色輪。

cues.text: Braxton: Okay, awesome, you glued this stuff and everything. This is fire.
cues.en: Braxton: Okay, awesome, you glued this stuff and everything. This is fire.
cues.zh: 布拉克斯頓：好吧，太棒了，你把這些東西和所有東西都黏在一起了。這是火。

cues.text: All twelve notes of the western musical scale are on it, but you might notice they’re a little mixed up
cues.en: All twelve notes of the western musical scale are on it, but you might notice they’re a little mixed up
cues.zh: 西方音階的所有十二個音符都在上面，但您可能會注意到它們有點混亂

cues.text: That’s because they’re organized by a very special number in music...
cues.en: That’s because they’re organized by a very special number in music...
cues.zh: 那是因為它們是由音樂中非常特殊的數字所組織的...

cues.text: a fifth.
cues.en: a fifth.
cues.zh: 第五個。

cues.text: What’s a fifth?
cues.en: What’s a fifth?
cues.zh: 什麼是五分之一？

cues.text: Braxton: It's like if you're in the C-major scale, you go C, D, E, F, G - right? 1,2,3,4,5.
cues.en: Braxton: It's like if you're in the C-major scale, you go C, D, E, F, G - right? 1,2,3,4,5.
cues.zh: Braxton：就像如果你在 C 大調音階中，你會選擇 C、D、E、F、G，對吧？ 1,2,3,4,5。

cues.text: From C to G is five notes, from G to D is five notes and… well you get the idea.
cues.en: From C to G is five notes, from G to D is five notes and… well you get the idea.
cues.zh: 從 C 到 G 是五個音符，從 G 到 D 是五個音符……好吧，你明白了。

cues.text: If you play through the circle you’ll traverse the entire keyboard starting on the lowest
cues.en: If you play through the circle you’ll traverse the entire keyboard starting on the lowest
cues.zh: 如果您彈奏整個圓圈，您將從最低的鍵盤開始遍歷整個鍵盤

cues.text: C and ending up on the highest C.
cues.en: C and ending up on the highest C.
cues.zh: C 並最終到達最高的 C。

cues.text: It sounds much more harmonious than just playing all the notes in order.
cues.en: It sounds much more harmonious than just playing all the notes in order.
cues.zh: 這聽起來比按順序演奏所有音符要和諧得多。

cues.text: That’s because...
cues.en: That’s because...
cues.zh: 那是因為...

cues.text: Adam: The fifth is a sound that our ears just like.
cues.en: Adam: The fifth is a sound that our ears just like.
cues.zh: Adam：第五個是我們耳朵喜歡的聲音。

cues.text: Uh... please explain.
cues.en: Uh... please explain.
cues.zh: 呃……請解釋一下。

cues.text: Adam: Whenever we're hearing anything, whenever we're hearing people sing...
cues.en: Adam: Whenever we're hearing anything, whenever we're hearing people sing...
cues.zh: 亞當：每當我們聽到任何聲音，每當我們聽到人們唱歌...

cues.text: Adam: Whenever we're hearing people play music, we're hearing these other notes, these overtones
cues.en: Adam: Whenever we're hearing people play music, we're hearing these other notes, these overtones
cues.zh: 亞當：每當我們聽到人們演奏音樂時，我們都會聽到這些其他音符，這些泛音

cues.text: alongside the pitches that they're playing.
cues.en: alongside the pitches that they're playing.
cues.zh: 在他們正在打的球場旁。

cues.text: When I play this C, the first two loudest tones that are pushed through the air are both C,
cues.en: When I play this C, the first two loudest tones that are pushed through the air are both C,
cues.zh: 當我彈奏這支C時，空氣中最響亮的前兩個音都是C，

cues.text: one is just an octave higher.
cues.en: one is just an octave higher.
cues.zh: 一個僅高一個八度。

cues.text: But other tones travel to our ears as well.
cues.en: But other tones travel to our ears as well.
cues.zh: 但其他音調也會傳入我們的耳朵。

cues.text: The third loudest is a G, which happens to be a fifth above C.
cues.en: The third loudest is a G, which happens to be a fifth above C.
cues.zh: 第三個響亮的是 G，它恰好比 C 高五度。

cues.text: In 1973, Leonard Bernstein demonstrated this phenomenon live on a grand piano at Harvard.
cues.en: In 1973, Leonard Bernstein demonstrated this phenomenon live on a grand piano at Harvard.
cues.zh: 1973 年，Leonard Bernstein 在哈佛大學的一架三角鋼琴上現場示範了這一現象。

cues.text: Listen closely after he hits that note.
cues.en: Listen closely after he hits that note.
cues.zh: 當他敲出那個音符後，仔細聽。

cues.text: Bernstein: What do we hear now? That G, right? A new tone.
cues.en: Bernstein: What do we hear now? That G, right? A new tone.
cues.zh: 伯恩斯坦：我們現在聽到什麼？那個G吧？新的基調。

cues.text: Again, clear as a bell. You want to hear it again?
cues.en: Again, clear as a bell. You want to hear it again?
cues.zh: 再次，清晰如鐘。你想再聽一次嗎？

cues.text: Adam: These overtones are kind of like subliminal tones that you're hearing alongside a regular note.
cues.en: Adam: These overtones are kind of like subliminal tones that you're hearing alongside a regular note.
cues.zh: Adam：這些泛音有點像你在常規音符旁邊聽到的潛意識音調。

cues.text: Adam: And you're hearing these overtones everywhere.
cues.en: Adam: And you're hearing these overtones everywhere.
cues.zh: 亞當：你到處都能聽到這些暗示。

cues.text: A lot of western music is based on the power of the fifth, especially how it relates so strongly back to its home chord.
cues.en: A lot of western music is based on the power of the fifth, especially how it relates so strongly back to its home chord.
cues.zh: 許多西方音樂都是基於五度音的力量，尤其是它與主和絃的緊密聯絡。

cues.text: Adam: In the case of the key of C major we have the G chord resolving to C.
cues.en: Adam: In the case of the key of C major we have the G chord resolving to C.
cues.zh: Adam：就 C 大調而言，G 和絃解析為 C。

cues.text: Adam: And if you’re thinking about what the G chord represents, it represents kind of tension. You want this to resolve.
cues.en: Adam: And if you’re thinking about what the G chord represents, it represents kind of tension. You want this to resolve.
cues.zh: Adam：如果你思考 G 和絃代表什麼，它代表一種緊張。你想要解決這個問題。

cues.text: When it finally does resolve, Adam: it creates this feeling of finality, it creates a feeling of home.
cues.en: When it finally does resolve, Adam: it creates this feeling of finality, it creates a feeling of home.
cues.zh: 當它最終解決時，亞當：它創造了這種最終的感覺，它創造了一種家的感覺。

cues.text: That five to one relationship is present in a lot of chord progressions, including the
cues.en: That five to one relationship is present in a lot of chord progressions, including the
cues.zh: 這種五對一的關係存在於許多和絃進行中，包括

cues.text: most common one found in jazz.
cues.en: most common one found in jazz.
cues.zh: 爵士樂中最常見的一種。

cues.text: The 2-5-1 Braxton:] The 2-5-1 essentially is like the backbone of most jazz music.
cues.en: The 2-5-1 Braxton:] The 2-5-1 essentially is like the backbone of most jazz music.
cues.zh: 2-5-1 Braxton：] 2-5-1 本質上就像大多數爵士樂的支柱。

cues.text: Even in its most basic form it sounds super jazzy.
cues.en: Even in its most basic form it sounds super jazzy.
cues.zh: 即使是最基本的形式，它聽起來也超級爵士。

cues.text: So it comes as no surprise the Coltrane Changes are just chock full of them.
cues.en: So it comes as no surprise the Coltrane Changes are just chock full of them.
cues.zh: 因此，Coltrane 的變化充滿了這些變化也就不足為奇了。

cues.text: Which might raise the question: Why was Tommy Flanagan caught off guard when he had
cues.en: Which might raise the question: Why was Tommy Flanagan caught off guard when he had
cues.zh: 這可能會提出一個問題：為什麼湯米·弗拉納根（Tommy Flanagan）在

cues.text: to improvise over them?
cues.en: to improvise over them?
cues.zh: 即興創作？

cues.text: Well, the Coltrane Changes aren’t in one key, they’re in three keys.
cues.en: Well, the Coltrane Changes aren’t in one key, they’re in three keys.
cues.zh: 嗯，Coltrane 的變化不是一鍵的，而是三鍵的。

cues.text: They’re basically a musical MC Escher painting.
cues.en: They’re basically a musical MC Escher painting.
cues.zh: 它們基本上是 MC Escher 的音樂畫作。

cues.text: So each one of these rungs on the circle of fifths represents every possible key center.
cues.en: So each one of these rungs on the circle of fifths represents every possible key center.
cues.zh: 因此，五度圓上的每一個梯級都代表每一個可能的調中心。

cues.text: The closer a key is to another, the more notes they have in common.
cues.en: The closer a key is to another, the more notes they have in common.
cues.zh: 一個調與另一個調越接近，它們的共同點就越多。

cues.text: Like the C major and G major scale - they’re only different by one note, an F#.
cues.en: Like the C major and G major scale - they’re only different by one note, an F#.
cues.zh: 就像 C 大調和 G 大調音階一樣 - 它們只存在一個音符不同，即 F#。

cues.text: Okay, we need an analogy to describe this.
cues.en: Okay, we need an analogy to describe this.
cues.zh: 好吧，我們需要一個類比來描述這一點。

cues.text: Adam: So the way that I like to think about keys is kind of like languages that you have to learn as a jazz improviser.
cues.en: Adam: So the way that I like to think about keys is kind of like languages that you have to learn as a jazz improviser.
cues.zh: Adam：所以我喜歡思考調性的方式有點像爵士即興演奏者必須學習的語言。

cues.text: You have to be able to be fluent in a key.
cues.en: You have to be able to be fluent in a key.
cues.zh: 您必須能夠流利地使用某個調。

cues.text: Like maybe C is Spanish and G is Portuguese.
cues.en: Like maybe C is Spanish and G is Portuguese.
cues.zh: 就像也許 C 是西班牙語，G 是葡萄牙語。

cues.text: Those are very similar languages.
cues.en: Those are very similar languages.
cues.zh: 這些都是非常相似的語言。

cues.text: Adam: If that's the case, like okay maybe C is Spanish and you have a distantly
cues.en: Adam: If that's the case, like okay maybe C is Spanish and you have a distantly
cues.zh: Adam：如果是這樣的話，好吧，也許 C 是西班牙語，而你有一個遙遠的

cues.text: related language like maybe Japanese.
cues.en: related language like maybe Japanese.
cues.zh: 相關語言，例如日語。

cues.text: Let’s say Japanese is B. There’s not much in common with those two languages. And it’s
cues.en: Let’s say Japanese is B. There’s not much in common with those two languages. And it’s
cues.zh: 假設日文是 B。這兩種語言沒有太多共同點。這是

cues.text: the same with keys. If you play those scales over each other...
cues.en: the same with keys. If you play those scales over each other...
cues.zh: 與鑰匙相同。如果你互相演奏這些音階......

cues.text: It sounds a lot more discordant.
cues.en: It sounds a lot more discordant.
cues.zh: 聽起來更不和諧。

cues.text: Adam: For the most part, most pop music is based around one of these key centers.
cues.en: Adam: For the most part, most pop music is based around one of these key centers.
cues.zh: Adam：在很大程度上，大多數流行音樂都是基於這些關鍵中心之一。

cues.text: For instance, Carly Rae Jepsen's “Cut to the Feeling” is in A major.
cues.en: For instance, Carly Rae Jepsen's “Cut to the Feeling” is in A major.
cues.zh: 例如，卡莉·雷·傑普森 (Carly Rae Jepsen) 的“Cut to the Feeling”就是 A 大調。

cues.text: But some songs modulate to another key for dramatic effect.
cues.en: But some songs modulate to another key for dramatic effect.
cues.zh: 但有些歌曲會調製到另一個調以獲得戲劇性的效果。

cues.text: Like Beyonce’s “Love on Top.” Adam: Part of the reason why it's really exciting is because you're going
cues.en: Like Beyonce’s “Love on Top.” Adam: Part of the reason why it's really exciting is because you're going
cues.zh: 就像碧昂絲的「愛在上面」。亞當：這真的令人興奮的部分原因是因為你要去

cues.text: to a place that's really distant on the circle of fifths.
cues.en: to a place that's really distant on the circle of fifths.
cues.zh: 到五度圈上一個非常遙遠的地方。

cues.text: And you’re creating a new sense of home. Which is exactly what “Love on Top” does.
cues.en: And you’re creating a new sense of home. Which is exactly what “Love on Top” does.
cues.zh: 您正在創造一種新的家的感覺。這正是「愛在上面」所做的。

cues.text: But, it doesn’t just happen once, it happens every time she repeats the chorus towards the
cues.en: But, it doesn’t just happen once, it happens every time she repeats the chorus towards the
cues.zh: 但是，這種事不只發生一次，每次她重複合唱時都會發生。

cues.text: end of the song.
cues.en: end of the song.
cues.zh: 歌曲結束。

cues.text: Adam: And when you chart that sort of thing along the circle of fifths, patterns emerge.
cues.en: Adam: And when you chart that sort of thing along the circle of fifths, patterns emerge.
cues.zh: 亞當：當你沿著五度圈繪製這類事物時，模式就會出現。

cues.text: These types of patterns are what fascinated John Coltrane in the late 1950s and '60s as
cues.en: These types of patterns are what fascinated John Coltrane in the late 1950s and '60s as
cues.zh: 這些型別的圖案在 20 世紀 50 年代末和 60 年代令 John Coltrane 著迷，因為

cues.text: he was trying to push jazz harmony to its limits.
cues.en: he was trying to push jazz harmony to its limits.
cues.zh: 他試圖將爵士樂和聲推向極限。

cues.text: This is his study of the circle of fifths.
cues.en: This is his study of the circle of fifths.
cues.zh: 這是他對五度圈的研究。

cues.text: Braxton: I think what makes Giant Steps really special is that it really just, it just documented an artist doing something super unique,
cues.en: Braxton: I think what makes Giant Steps really special is that it really just, it just documented an artist doing something super unique,
cues.zh: 布拉克斯頓：我認為《巨人的腳步》真正特別的地方在於，它只是記錄了藝術家所做的一些超級獨特的事情，

cues.text: super stylistic, and virtuosic at the same time.
cues.en: super stylistic, and virtuosic at the same time.
cues.zh: 超級風格，同時也是精湛的。

cues.text: Here’s the first 16 bars of Giant Steps again, with just the key changes highlighted.
cues.en: Here’s the first 16 bars of Giant Steps again, with just the key changes highlighted.
cues.zh: 這是 Giant Steps 的前 16 小節，僅突出顯示了關鍵的變化。

cues.text: If you chart those changes on the circle of fifths it comes out as a pretty dramatic pattern.
cues.en: If you chart those changes on the circle of fifths it comes out as a pretty dramatic pattern.
cues.zh: 如果你把這些變化畫在五度圈上，你會發現這是一個非常戲劇性的模式。

cues.text: That’s because these keys are separated by major thirds, which divide an octave into
cues.en: That’s because these keys are separated by major thirds, which divide an octave into
cues.zh: 這是因為這些鍵被大三度分開，大三度將一個八度分成

cues.text: 3 equal parts.
cues.en: 3 equal parts.
cues.zh: 3等份。

cues.text: On the circle of fifths these three keys are as far apart as possible from each other.
cues.en: On the circle of fifths these three keys are as far apart as possible from each other.
cues.zh: 在五度圈上，這三個鍵彼此之間的距離盡可能遠。

cues.text: Adam: Giant Steps is kind of like you're shifting from Spanish to Arabic to Japanese
cues.en: Adam: Giant Steps is kind of like you're shifting from Spanish to Arabic to Japanese
cues.zh: Adam：Giant Steps 有點像你從西班牙語轉向阿拉伯語再到日語

cues.text: very quickly.
cues.en: very quickly.
cues.zh: 非常快。

cues.text: By quickly, he means like every two beats in a song that’s nearly 300 bpm.
cues.en: By quickly, he means like every two beats in a song that’s nearly 300 bpm.
cues.zh: 他所說的「快」是指一首近 300 bpm 的歌曲中的每兩個節拍。

cues.text: Adam: It's not only just like you're saying one word per language, you're having to construct
cues.en: Adam: It's not only just like you're saying one word per language, you're having to construct
cues.zh: Adam：這不僅僅是你對每種語言說一個單詞，你還必須構建

cues.text: a sentence out of the language.
cues.en: a sentence out of the language.
cues.zh: 語言之外的一句話。

cues.text: And how does Coltrane make those disparate languages connect? With one of the most ubiquitous
cues.en: And how does Coltrane make those disparate languages connect? With one of the most ubiquitous
cues.zh: Coltrane 如何將這些不同的語言連結起來？與最普遍的之一

cues.text: phrases in jazz, the five one.
cues.en: phrases in jazz, the five one.
cues.zh: 爵士樂中的樂句，五一。

cues.text: Adam: What he's doing is taking some of the conventional ideas of tonal harmony,
cues.en: Adam: What he's doing is taking some of the conventional ideas of tonal harmony,
cues.zh: 亞當：他正在做的是採用一些傳統的音調和諧概念，

cues.text: the conventional relationships between the five chord and the one chord and applying it to this very chaotic circling,
cues.en: the conventional relationships between the five chord and the one chord and applying it to this very chaotic circling,
cues.zh: 五和絃與一和絃之間的傳統關係並將其應用於這個非常混亂的迴圈，

cues.text: sort of chord progression that is the Coltrane Changes.
cues.en: sort of chord progression that is the Coltrane Changes.
cues.zh: 一種和絃進行，即 Coltrane 變化。

cues.text: Adam: So if we were all in the same key, it would sound like this.
cues.en: Adam: So if we were all in the same key, it would sound like this.
cues.zh: Adam：所以如果我們都用同一個調，聽起來就會像這樣。

cues.text: Adam: But because we're going from key center to key center, it sounds very different.
cues.en: Adam: But because we're going from key center to key center, it sounds very different.
cues.zh: Adam：但是因為我們要從一個關鍵中心轉到另一個關鍵中心，所以聽起來很不同。

cues.text: This is why the Coltrane Changes are like this picture here.
cues.en: This is why the Coltrane Changes are like this picture here.
cues.zh: 這就是為什麼 Coltrane 的變化就像這張圖一樣。

cues.text: Even though you’re seeing things from a completely new perspective you still feel
cues.en: Even though you’re seeing things from a completely new perspective you still feel
cues.zh: 即使你從一個全新的角度看待事物，你仍然感覺

cues.text: like you’ve made it home somehow.
cues.en: like you’ve made it home somehow.
cues.zh: 就像你已經以某種方式回到家一樣。

cues.text: When Tommy Flanagan saw the charts for Giant Steps he knew he wasn’t going to just have
cues.en: When Tommy Flanagan saw the charts for Giant Steps he knew he wasn’t going to just have
cues.zh: 當湯米·弗拉納根 (Tommy Flanagan) 看到 Giant Steps 的圖表時，他知道他不會僅僅擁有

cues.text: to play this chord progression - he was going to have to improvise over it.
cues.en: to play this chord progression - he was going to have to improvise over it.
cues.zh: 為了演奏這個和絃進行——他必須即興創作。

cues.text: very quickly.
cues.en: very quickly.
cues.zh: 非常快。

cues.text: Braxton: That was probably so funny, he was probably like, "What?!" Adam: It is a bit of a rite of passage to say that you not only can improvise on Giant Steps,
cues.en: Braxton: That was probably so funny, he was probably like, "What?!" Adam: It is a bit of a rite of passage to say that you not only can improvise on Giant Steps,
cues.zh: 布拉克斯頓：這可能很有趣，他可能會說，「什麼？！」亞當：說你不僅可以在巨型臺階上即興發揮，這有點像是一種成年儀式，

cues.text: but you can also improvise in all 12 keys.
cues.en: but you can also improvise in all 12 keys.
cues.zh: 但您也可以即興演奏全部 12 個按鍵。

cues.text: Adam: Now, generations of jazz musicians are approaching Giant Steps as the sort of pinnacle of improvisation.
cues.en: Adam: Now, generations of jazz musicians are approaching Giant Steps as the sort of pinnacle of improvisation.
cues.zh: 亞當：現在，一代又一代的爵士音樂家正在將「巨人階梯」視為即興創作的頂峰。

cues.text: Wait. I think I’ve got an analogy for this. It’s like you’re a cab driver and instead
cues.en: Wait. I think I’ve got an analogy for this. It’s like you’re a cab driver and instead
cues.zh: 等待。我想我對此有一個類比。這就像你是計程車司機，而不是

cues.text: of only knowing one way to get somewhere, you have to know every back alley and side
cues.en: of only knowing one way to get somewhere, you have to know every back alley and side
cues.zh: 只知道去某個地方的一種方法，你必須知道每一個後巷和側面

cues.text: street just in case.
cues.en: street just in case.
cues.zh: 街上以防萬一。

cues.text: Braxton: It's essentially like that. You still get to the same location, but it’s really interesting and you might see
cues.en: Braxton: It's essentially like that. You still get to the same location, but it’s really interesting and you might see
cues.zh: 布拉克斯頓：本質上就是這樣。你仍然到達相同的位置，但這真的很有趣，你可能會看到

cues.text: some really cool stuff in the neighborhood.
cues.en: some really cool stuff in the neighborhood.
cues.zh: 附近有一些非常酷的東西。

cues.text: Braxton: But ultimately I still think the music boils down to 5 1. People want to come
cues.en: Braxton: But ultimately I still think the music boils down to 5 1. People want to come
cues.zh: 布拉克斯頓：但最終我仍然認為音樂可以歸結為 5 1。人們想要來

cues.text: back home.
cues.en: back home.
cues.zh: 回到家。

cues.text: Thanks so much for watching the first of three videos I'm going to release in the next couple of weeks on Jazz.
cues.en: Thanks so much for watching the first of three videos I'm going to release in the next couple of weeks on Jazz.
cues.zh: 非常感謝您觀看我將在接下來的幾週內在 Jazz 上發布的三個影片中的第一個。

cues.text: I want to give a special thanks to Braxton Cook and Adam Neely.
cues.en: I want to give a special thanks to Braxton Cook and Adam Neely.
cues.zh: 我要特別感謝布拉克斯頓·庫克和亞當·尼利。

cues.en: Between the time that I interviewed Braxton and now, he's released a full album.
cues.zh: 從我採訪布拉克斯頓到現在，他發行了一張完整的專輯。

cues.en: Please check it out below and of course special, special thanks to Adam Neely.
